newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Swedish Dec CPI seen falling 0.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Swedish Dec CPI seen falling 0.3 pct.

text.p: Sweden's consumer price index (CPI) is expected to fall by 0.3 percent in December for a fall of 0.3 percent over the previous 12 months, a Reuters poll of 10 analysts showed on Wednesday.
Forecasts for the December change varied between a fall of 0.2 and 0.5 percent.
For calendar 1996 Sweden's inflation rate was expected to come in at 0.7 percent, according to economists, with forecasts ranging from 0.5 to 0.8 percent.
Sweden's official statistics bureau Statistics Sweden will publish the CPI for December on January 21 at 0815 GMT.
In 1995 the rate of inflation on average was 2.9 percent.
In November the Swedish CPI fell 0.3 percent which gave a 12 month fall of 0.3 percent.
In December 1995 the CPI was 0.3 percent for a year figure of 2.6 percent.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Carnegie, Chase, Consensus, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland, Morgan Stanley, PaineWebber, S-E-Banken, Union Bank of Switzerland.
